events.ai_basis: A large language model (GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT) was used in a substantial way at all stages of this project.

why: The statement asks for the minimiser of the equal-volume partition problem and for Weaire–Phelan's optimality. The September 2026 parallelohedra theorems (Hales–Song; Cesaroni–Novaga) solve that same minimisation over a restricted class of partitions (translative tilings by one convex cell), which is a restriction of the question rather than a changed functional, so I scored them case; the authors' statement that this does not solve the Kelvin problem is consistent with case rather than whole. Local-minimality results (lattice Voronoi, parallelohedra) are weaker forms and are variant; different functionals, dimensions, unequal volumes or topology-restricted comparisons are variant; existence-only papers are none. Weaire–Phelan 1994 is a record construction beating Kelvin's foam, a bound on the minimal area, pre-snapshot. AI: Hales–Song say the model was used 'in a substantial way at all stages', and v2 (via a summary) mentions 'proof discovery'. The work is human-led and the authors take responsibility for it, so assisted rather than generated. Cesaroni–Novaga's model checked identities and 'assisted in exploring and verifying' arguments, which is checking and exploration and so none.
doubts: Hales–Song's AI quote is vague about what the model actually produced. 'Proof discovery' comes from a summarising fetch, not verbatim text. The assisted vs none call rests on it. Whether parallelohedra count as a case of the bullet or as a variant is a close call: I chose case because the problem stays the same (equal-volume, least area) over a subclass. Neither September preprint has been reviewed, and the Hales–Song certificate has not been replayed.
